title: The settings for the tool in your hand are reachable with the panel hidden
goal: Some things belong to the tool you are holding rather than to anything you have picked: how much a zoom callout magnifies and whether it is a box or a circle, how forgiving the wand is, what Measure snaps to and shows. Every one of them lives in the right hand panel today, so hiding the panel, which is a normal thing to do while you work on a picture, takes them all away. They move into a capsule that rides just above the floating tool bar, always open, showing whatever the tool in your hand has to set.
notes:
Design review 2026-09-04. Named as a house rule by the audit that added the newest one: queue/audits/2026-09-04-callout-shape.json rough 1 ("With the inspector hidden there is no way to the choice at all. Every other tool setting has the same gap (the wands tolerance, crops aspect), so this follows the house rule rather than fixing it"). queue/audits/2026-09-04-callout-one-home.json is the same story from the other side: the popover that used to hold tool settings was unreachable code, because picking up a drawing tool clears the layer selection, so the settings were moved into the panel with nowhere else to go. This is also a documented rule that reality has moved past: docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md section 6 says tool options are "shown in the options bar or the top of the Inspector", and there is no options bar in the app. Either build the strip the doc promises or change the doc; do not leave them disagreeing. Worth a decision card with shots before building, since it puts new chrome on screen.

Decision answered on 2026-09-05: option c, a capsule above the tool bar. Not the recommended option a (press and hold the tool button); the user chose always open and next to the button over hidden until asked. The cost they accepted, in their own card: it sits over the bottom of the picture, which on a screenshot is often where the buttons being redlined are. The mitigation that made it safe: it is its own capsule on its own row rather than part of the tool bar, so the tool bar never changes width, and the capsule wraps on a narrow window. That matters because tool settings used to live inside the tool bar and made it 150 to 200 points wider the moment you picked up Measure or Crop, and that was removed on purpose. Do not put them back in the bar.
acceptance: A capsule sits just above the floating tool bar carrying the settings for the tool in your hand, open without pressing anything
It is its own capsule on its own row, so the tool bar itself never changes width whichever tool you pick up
It shows nothing at all, and takes no room, for a tool with nothing to set, so picking the arrow does not leave an empty bar hanging there
It changes as the tool changes, and it works whether the right hand panel is shown or hidden
On a narrow window it wraps rather than running off the edge or pushing the tool bar off the picture
Nothing that belongs to a selected layer moves out of the right hand panel, and with the panel shown the panel keeps working exactly as it does now
The settings in the capsule and the same settings in the panel are one thing: changing either shows in both at once

Ships behind next-tool-settings. To see it: open Photonz Next, pick the Zoom Callout tool, hide the right hand panel with Option Command L, and change its shape from Rectangle to Circle in the capsule
The audit says how much of the picture the capsule covers at the bottom of a normal window, since that is the cost the user accepted when they picked this
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

Adversarial review, on the real app (probe, Next, Screen Recording granted). Walk: /tmp/pz/tool-settings-gap.json, shots in /tmp/photonz-playtest/tool-settings-gap.

The premise is partly wrong, and the correction matters. Crop's aspect and Measure's mode are NOT panel-only: those tool buttons wear a small corner wedge and press-and-hold lists the choice, so they survive the panel being hidden. Confirmed on a real capture of the bar with the panel hidden.

What is actually stranded when the panel is hidden: the Zoom Callout's Shape, the Magic Wand's Tolerance, and Measure's Snap and Show. The pattern is not tool-vs-panel, it is MODE-vs-SETTING: modes went into the tool button on 2026-08-23 (D15) and settings went to the panel, and only the settings half lost its way home.

So the shortest fix is not new chrome at all: give the tool button's existing flyout a settings foot, which D15 already sanctions in writing ("settings live in the Inspector ... or at the foot of the same flyout when they change how the next click behaves"). The wedge then appears on the wand and the callout too, which is exactly the rule the wedge already states: there is more inside this button.

Second finding: the panel does not only hide when you ask it to. EditorView.updateInspectorAutoCollapse hides it for you on a narrow window, so a person can lose the callout's Shape without ever having pressed anything.

Third finding, against Option A: the flyout is a real NSMenu (Menu(primaryAction:)), which takes Picker, Toggle, Button and Divider but not a Slider. The wand's Tolerance would have to become stepped choices or +/- rows there, which is a downgrade from the slider it has in the panel. Called out in the decision card rather than hidden.

Fourth finding: UX-PATTERNS section 6 line 291 still promises an "options bar", and D15 (line 1044) contradicts it. Whichever option wins, that line gets rewritten in the same change. Not fixed yet because the wording depends on the answer.

Waiting on the decision "With the right hand panel hidden, where should the settings for the tool in your hand live?" Four options with real shots of today's gap and sketches of each answer; recommended A (settings at the foot of the tool button's press-and-hold list, the gesture Crop and Measure already use). Nothing built, because every answer puts the controls somewhere different.
decision "With the right hand panel hidden, where should the settings for the tool in your hand live?" resolved: In a capsule above the tool bar
Triage: rewrote the goal and acceptance to the answered decision (capsule above the tool bar, option c).
claimed by go loop
Adversarial review before building. The decision is answered (capsule above the bar), so the question is not whether but what goes in it and what it collides with.

What belongs in it, and it is narrower than the goal's list. The goal names callout magnification, but magnification is a property of a callout you have already drawn (CalloutInspector), and acceptance says nothing belonging to a picked layer leaves the panel. So the capsule carries the four TOOL settings that are genuinely stranded: the callout tool's Shape, the wand's Tolerance, and Measure's Snap and Show. Crop's Aspect and Measure's Mode are modes and already survive a hidden panel inside the tool button's flyout, so putting them in the capsule would widen it for nothing.

Biggest real risk: the bottom of the canvas is already crowded. The Measure hint pill and the crop Cancel/Crop pill both park at EditorChromeLayout.aboveToolBar, which is exactly the band the capsule now takes, and the measure legend keeps clear of bottomChrome. Measure is one of the three tools WITH a capsule, so the hint would land on top of it on day one. Fix is to make the whole stack capsule-aware rather than to nudge one pill.

Second risk: the tool bar measures its own width through a background GeometryReader and that measurement drives the overflow loop. Putting the capsule in the same measured container would feed the bar the capsule's width and shed tools for no reason. The capsule goes in a VStack ABOVE the measured container, never inside it.

Shortest version that delivers the value: no new settings, no moving anything out of the panel. The panel keeps every tool section exactly as it is (acceptance says so), the capsule reads and writes the same EditorState properties, so the two are one thing for free rather than by a sync mechanism.

Accepted cost, to be measured in the audit: with the wand, the callout or Measure in hand the capsule covers a band across the bottom centre of the picture, which on a screenshot is often where the buttons being redlined are. Not mitigable beyond keeping it short: it is the cost the user chose over a hidden-until-asked control.

Duplication is deliberate: with the panel open Tolerance appears twice, once in the capsule and once in the Magic Wand section. Acceptance requires both, and they are one value, so this is a legibility question for the audit rather than a bug.

Built behind next-tool-settings, on by default in Next. New: PhotonzCore/ToolSettingsBar.swift (what each tool carries, and the row packing, both unit tested), EditorChromeLayout.aboveToolBar(toolSettingsHeight:) / toolSettingsFrame / bottomChrome's new toolSettingsSize, and Photonz/ToolSettingsCapsule.swift (the capsule and its wrapping Layout). EditorView stacks it above the bar in the canvas's bottom overlay.
Second adversarial review, on the real app (probe, Next, Screen Recording granted). Walks: Scripts/playtest/tool-settings-capsule-walk.json and tool-settings-narrow-walk.json.

Two real faults found and fixed on the running app. First: a maxWidth frame made the glass span the whole picture, 1248pt of capsule for a 214pt setting. The capsule now hugs its content and the wrap layout takes the offered width only as the line it wraps at. Second: an empty capsule is still a stack child, so the 12pt gap above it pushed the bar up off its own inset for a tool with nothing to set; the whole branch is now conditional.

Verified in numbers, not by eye. Bar measured 916.5pt with every tool, and the active tool circle sat on pixel rows 1572 to 1627 for select, callout and measure alike: the bar neither moves nor changes width. Capsule 214x36 (callout), 235.5x30 (wand), 340.5x36 (measure), 0x0 (select and every other tool).

Both directions of the one-value rule proved: changed Snap in the CAPSULE and the panel's Snap row followed to Edges; changed Show in the PANEL and the capsule followed to Spacing (panel dumps 7 and 8).

Click-through checked: with the callout in hand, a drag in the capsule's own vertical band but beside it still reaches the picture (layers 1 -> 2, then undone). The capsule takes no hit area it does not cover.

Wrapping is honest but unseen: the widest capsule is 340pt and the narrowest picture the app allows is 448pt across, so with today's three tools it never has to wrap. The packing is a pure function in PhotonzCore with five tests, so the next setting added cannot break it. Said plainly in the audit.

The animation is scoped: the stack springs the capsule in and out, and the tool bar carries .animation(nil, value: activeTool) so its accent circle keeps exactly the behaviour it had. Sliding the circle would have been a change to the bar nobody asked for.

Docs reconciled, which the task asked for: UX-PATTERNS section 6 and the tool strip line no longer promise an options bar that never existed, and D15 gained the rule for where a setting lives, with the 2026-09-05 decision and the reason the flyout option lost (a real NSMenu takes a picker but not a slider).

Follow-ups filed: choosing-how-much-a-callout-magnifies-before-you (the goal named magnification and it did not move, because it belongs to a drawn callout rather than to the tool) and a-tool-setting-that-is-on-screen-twice-reads-as (whether the panel section should stand down while the capsule is up, which is the user's call).
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-05-tool-settings.json with three real screen captures. Scripts/test.sh green, 3512 tests.

The settings for the tool in hand ride in their own capsule above the floating tool bar, behind next-tool-settings (on by default in Next): callout Shape, wand Tolerance, Measure Snap and Show. New PhotonzCore/ToolSettingsBar.swift (contents + row packing, unit tested), EditorChromeLayout capsule-aware bottom chrome, Photonz/ToolSettingsCapsule.swift. Verified on the running probe with Screen Recording granted: bar stayed 916.5pt and its accent circle on the same pixel row for every tool, capsule 0x0 for tools with nothing to set, both directions of the shared-value rule proved from the panel dumps, and a drag beside the capsule still reaches the picture. Scripts/test.sh green, 3512 tests. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-05-tool-settings.json with three real captures; UX-PATTERNS reconciled; two follow-ups filed.
